title: Lord, When I Count Thy Mercies O'er
description: Lord, When I Count Thy Mercies O'er in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 139, part 6, headed “The mercies of God innumerable”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Lord, when I count thy mer-cies o'er, They strike me with sur-prise; Not all the sands that spread the shore To e-qual num-bers rise.

lines: Lord, when I count thy mercies o'er,
Not all the sands that spread the shore
My flesh with fear and wonder stands,
And hourly blessings from thy hands,
These on my heart by night I keep;
How kind, how dear to me!
O may the hour that ends my sleep
Still find my thoughts with thee.

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
